geography.notes: Available only to qualifying Aiken Electric Cooperative residential members at served premises.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be an active Aiken Electric Cooperative member.
Equipment must be at the member's primary residence served by Aiken Electric Cooperative.
Member must own the property where the water heater or timer is installed.
Member must sign the program agreement and keep eligible equipment active for the required term.
blockers: Smart thermostat incentives are on a separate Aiken Electric Cooperative Ecobee program and should not match this water-heater opportunity.
Non-residential structures are not eligible for this residential water-heater program.
Unsupported HVAC, thermostat, or general weatherization categories should be removed.
repairs.evidenceText: The official water-heater page supports Aiken's residential water heater and timer program; smart thermostat incentives are addressed on a separate Ecobee page.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The supplied thermostat match is a false positive for this DSIRE record because the current official URL is a water-heater program, not the separate thermostat program.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying residential Alabama Power electric-service accounts.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be an active residential Alabama Power customer.
Thermostat must be new, installed at the Alabama Power service address, and on the qualifying-products list.
Application must be submitted within one year of thermostat purchase.
Proof of purchase must show purchase date, brand, model, amount paid, and payment method.
Homeowner approval is required when the customer is not the owner.
blockers: Multifamily apartments do not qualify.
Accounts that already received a free thermostat or prior smart thermostat rebate are not eligible.
Taxes, shipping, installation, used equipment, and nonqualifying models are not reimbursed.
repairs.evidenceText: Alabama Power's rebate page and reimbursement form support an eligible smart thermostat reimbursement for active residential customers using qualifying models.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The smart thermostat match is source-backed and should remain limited to residential Alabama Power customers and qualifying thermostat products.

geography.notes: Statewide New Mexico tax credit for approved manufacturing operations.

hardRequirements: Credit applies to qualified manufacturing equipment used in manufacturing alternative energy products.
Applicant must receive approval before claiming the credit.
Applicant must satisfy statutory employment-addition requirements tied to qualified expenditures.
Claim is made through New Mexico tax forms after approval.
blockers: This is not a rebate or tax credit for installing a fuel cell system at a building.
Fuel cells are referenced as manufactured products, not as eligible customer retrofit equipment.
General clean-energy installation, residential, or commercial building retrofit matches should be blocked.
repairs.administrator: New Mexico Economic Development Department and New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department
repairs.evidenceText: The official application describes a credit for manufacturing equipment used to produce alternative energy products, including fuel cell systems as products.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The fuel cell match is deterministic noise because eligibility is for manufacturers' production equipment, not end-use fuel-cell retrofits.

geography.notes: Statewide Pennsylvania consumer vehicle rebate; funding is first-come and limited.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be a Pennsylvania resident.
Application must be submitted no later than six months after eligible vehicle purchase.
Vehicle must meet final purchase-price and eligible-fuel requirements.
Companies, nonprofits, and government entities are directed to the separate Alternative Fuels Incentive Grant program.
blockers: This rebate is for purchasing eligible alternative fuel vehicles, not installing stationary fuel cell systems.
Building energy, fuel-cell generation, EV charging, and refueling equipment categories should not match this opportunity.
Program remains limited by available rebate funds.
repairs.evidenceText: Pennsylvania DEP identifies this as a consumer rebate for eligible alternative fuel vehicles, with limited remaining funds and vehicle purchase requirements.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The fuel-cell term refers to possible vehicle fuel types, not stationary fuel-cell retrofit eligibility.

geography.notes: Federal credit was limited to qualifying property in eligible census tracts and placed in service before July 1, 2026.

hardRequirements: Business-use property must be depreciable and used primarily in the United States or its territories.
Original use of the refueling property must begin with the taxpayer.
Property must be in an eligible low-income or non-urban census tract.
Qualified property had to be placed in service before July 1, 2026.
Prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements are needed for the 30 percent business credit rate.
blockers: New projects placed in service after June 30, 2026 are outside the current federal eligibility window.
Property outside eligible census tracts does not qualify.
This credit should not match general EV purchases or unrelated building electrification.
repairs.evidenceText: IRS guidance supports EV charging and alternative refueling property but limits eligibility to property placed in service before July 1, 2026.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The EV charger category is substantively correct, but the opportunity should be unavailable for new post-deadline projects as of the research date.

geography.notes: Federal personal credit was limited to main-home installations in eligible census tracts and property placed in service before July 1, 2026.

hardRequirements: Personal-use property must be installed at the taxpayer's main home.
Original use of the refueling property must begin with the taxpayer.
Property must be in an eligible low-income or non-urban census tract.
Qualified property had to be placed in service before July 1, 2026.
blockers: New personal EV charger installations placed in service after June 30, 2026 are outside the current credit window.
Second homes and locations outside eligible census tracts do not qualify.
This credit should not match vehicle purchases or unrelated home energy measures.
repairs.evidenceText: IRS guidance supports a personal credit for qualifying EV charging or refueling property, but only for property placed in service before July 1, 2026.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The EV charger category is correct historically, but availability is expired for new residential projects as of 2026-07-02.

geography.notes: Initial Arkansas NEVI funding is targeted to designated EV Alternative Fuel Corridors and eligible public or commercial-motor-vehicle charging locations.

hardRequirements: Project must be directly associated with charging electric vehicles.
Charging infrastructure must be open to the public or to authorized commercial motor vehicle operators from more than one company.
Applicant must meet Arkansas NEVI proposer eligibility requirements.
Projects are reimbursed with federal funds up to the allowed share and require non-federal match.
Projects must meet federal NEVI and ARDOT technical and location requirements.
blockers: Private residential chargers are not eligible.
Single-company fleet-only charging that is not available to more than one commercial operator is not eligible.
Funding depends on competitive solicitation timing and approved locations.
repairs.evidenceText: ARDOT NEVI materials support grants for eligible public EV charging infrastructure, not private home charging.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The EV charging match is correct only for NEVI-compliant public or qualifying commercial charging infrastructure.

geography.notes: Available within the City of Ashland electric utility service territory.

hardRequirements: Solar electric system must be interconnected to Ashland electric service and net-metered.
System must include at least 2,500 watts of panels with required solar access.
Required city permits, inspections, application, purchase agreement, roof plan, and invoice documentation must be submitted.
Owner of the system must own or be a tenant of the facility where the system is installed.
blockers: Systems installed outside Ashland electric service territory do not qualify.
Solar thermal, battery storage, and non-PV measures are not supported by this PV rebate.
Systems removed or inactive before the required operating period may trigger repayment.
repairs.evidenceText: Ashland's solar page and application materials support a city electric utility incentive for new grid-connected solar electric systems.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The photovoltaic match is source-backed; the category is broadened from rooftop-only to solar PV because official materials allow solar electric systems generally.

geography.notes: Statewide New Jersey farmland-assessment treatment through local municipal assessors.

hardRequirements: Property must otherwise qualify and remain in agricultural or horticultural use.
Energy generated must be used to provide power or heat to the farm.
Acreage and generation caps apply, including the one-acre-to-five-acre ratio and maximum limits.
A conservation plan and required approvals must be filed with the municipal assessor.
Biomass systems require New Jersey Department of Agriculture approval.
blockers: This is farmland property-tax assessment treatment, not a rebate or installation grant.
Renewable systems primarily serving non-farm uses or general power-sale projects should not match.
Income from selling power or heat is not farm income for farmland-assessment qualification.
repairs.administrator: New Jersey Division of Taxation and municipal assessors
repairs.evidenceText: New Jersey farmland-assessment materials identify biomass, solar, and wind systems as potentially eligible when tied to qualifying farm use.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The biomass match is supported, but matching must enforce agricultural land-use, power-use, acreage, and approval constraints.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying commercial Austin Energy electric accounts.

hardRequirements: Applicant must have an Austin Energy commercial electric account.
Project must use an Austin Energy participating solar contractor.
Application must be approved before installation or financial commitment.
Third-party power purchase agreements are not allowed.
PBI eligibility and rate level depend on system AC size and program rules.
blockers: This PBI is not a one-time commercial cash rebate; Austin Energy's commercial CBI is a separate option.
Residential and multifamily solar projects should use their separate Austin Energy programs.
Projects installed before approval are not eligible.
repairs.evidenceText: Austin Energy's business solar page supports a commercial solar PBI option with bill credits for on-site solar generation.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The solar PV match is source-backed, but this record should remain distinct from Austin Energy's commercial capacity-based rebate.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying commercial Austin Energy electric accounts.

hardRequirements: Applicant must have an Austin Energy commercial electric account.
Project must use an Austin Energy participating solar contractor.
Application and letter of intent must be completed before installation.
Third-party power purchase agreements are not allowed.
System size, customer type, and incentive caps determine CBI amount.
blockers: This CBI is the upfront commercial incentive, not the performance-based incentive record.
Residential and multifamily solar projects are separate Austin Energy programs.
Projects installed before approval or using nonparticipating contractors are not eligible.
repairs.evidenceText: Austin Energy's business solar page supports an upfront commercial capacity-based incentive for eligible on-site solar installations.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The solar PV match is source-backed; matching must distinguish this CBI from the separate PBI.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying multifamily properties served by Austin Energy.

hardRequirements: Property must be a qualifying multifamily property in Austin Energy service territory.
Project must use a participating Austin Energy solar contractor.
Application and letter of intent must be completed before installation.
Incentive generally applies to residentially metered multifamily units.
Funding is limited and available on a first-come basis.
blockers: Commercial, master-metered, office, and common-area projects are directed to the commercial solar program.
Leased systems and third-party power purchase agreements are not eligible.
Single-family residential solar should use the residential rebate program.
repairs.evidenceText: Austin Energy's multifamily solar materials support a capacity-based incentive for qualifying multifamily properties using participating contractors.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying Austin Energy residential electric customers.

hardRequirements: Applicant must have an Austin Energy residential electric account.
New solar system must be installed at the account premise.

repairs.reasoningNotes: The solar PV match is source-backed and should stay limited to Austin Energy residential solar installations.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying Austin Utilities residential customers.

hardRequirements: House Call energy audit is required for listed weatherization rebates.
Rebated work must be recommended through the audit.
Work must be completed by a qualified participating contractor when required.

geography.notes: Available for qualifying buildings and homes located in Baltimore County.

hardRequirements: Applicant must submit the county tax-credit application and required certification documentation by the stated June 1 deadline.
Commercial high performance buildings must meet at least LEED Silver under applicable LEED rating systems.
High performance homes require certified LEED rating documentation from a qualified rater.
A property owner may receive only one high performance credit per building.
blockers: This is a property tax credit tied to green building certification, not a direct rebate for individual measures.
Buildings without qualifying LEED or accepted high-performance certification documentation do not qualify.
The credit may terminate if the building is altered so it no longer complies with the rating basis.
repairs.administrator: Baltimore County Office of Budget and Finance
repairs.evidenceText: Baltimore County materials support property tax credits for high performance buildings and homes based on LEED rating documentation.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The LEED match is supported, but official pages were partially blocked from direct fetch; search snippets and official PDFs were sufficient for core eligibility.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying non-residential SCE customers in SCE service territory.

hardRequirements: Customer must be a non-residential SCE customer with required interval metering.
Business must have registered demand reaching or exceeding 200 kW.
Customer must select a firm service level and 15- or 30-minute response option.
Customer must commit to reducing demand by at least 15 percent and at least 100 kW during events.
BIP events may occur year-round and are limited by tariff event rules.
blockers: BIP is a demand response enrollment and bill-credit tariff, not an incentive for automated demand response controls.
Auto-DR technology incentives are a separate SCE program and should not be inferred from BIP.
Residential customers and businesses below BIP demand thresholds are not eligible.
repairs.evidenceText: SCE describes BIP as a non-residential demand response bill-credit program for customers able to reduce load during events.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The matched automated controls category should be removed because BIP does not itself fund or require a physical controls retrofit.

geography.notes: Statewide Maine property tax exemption or reimbursement treatment for qualifying business equipment.

hardRequirements: Battery storage must qualify as business equipment used exclusively for a business purpose.
Equipment must satisfy Maine BETE placed-in-service and depreciation requirements.
More than 50 percent of battery output must serve load behind the utility meter, or the battery owner must have had a fully executed utility interconnection agreement by January 1, 2025.
Application must be filed annually with the appropriate assessor or Maine Revenue Services by the applicable deadline.
blockers: Residential batteries and personal-use equipment do not qualify under BETE business equipment rules.
Property owned by excluded persons or exempt under another property-tax provision may be ineligible.
General office lighting, building-serving equipment, vehicles, and unrelated business equipment should not match this battery-storage record.
repairs.evidenceText: Maine law and Revenue Services materials expressly include qualifying battery storage systems in business equipment exemption or reimbursement treatment.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The battery storage match is source-backed, but only for qualifying business equipment under the current Maine statutory limits.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying commercial electric customers in Beaches Energy Services service territory.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be a commercial electric customer of Beaches Energy Services.

Customer must contact the conservation specialist before installation.
Retrofit worksheet and lighting analysis must be completed and reviewed before installation.
Work must be completed by a licensed Florida contractor with required permits.
Application must be submitted within 90 days of purchase or installation.
blockers: New construction commercial properties are not eligible.
Non-lighting measures should not match this commercial lighting rebate.
Residential lighting products are not covered by this commercial lighting rebate.
Rebate will not exceed purchase price and may be altered or canceled without notice.
repairs.evidenceText: Beaches Energy lists a commercial lighting rebate and the form supports energy-efficient lighting upgrades for existing commercial properties.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The LED lighting match is source-backed, but should be limited to existing commercial lighting upgrades in Beaches Energy territory.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying residential retail electric customers in Beaches Energy Services service territory.

hardRequirements: Applicant must be a residential retail electric customer of Beaches Energy Services.
Equipment must be Florida Solar Energy Center certified solar domestic water heating equipment.
System must replace an electric hot water heater.
System components must be new and not rebuilt, refurbished, relocated, or previously placed in service.

System must be at least 80 percent shade-free and guaranteed against freeze damage.

blockers: Solar pool heating systems, including spas and commercial or institutional pool systems, are ineligible.

Commercial, institutional, non-domestic, non-solar, and heat-pump water heaters should not match this record.
Only one rebate per residential customer account is allowed.
repairs.evidenceText: Beaches Energy's solar water heater form supports a residential rebate for certified solar domestic water heaters replacing electric water heaters.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The solar water heating match is source-backed and should remain product-specific; it should not generalize to pool heating or non-solar water heaters.

geography.notes: Available to qualifying Belmont Light residential customers or eligible property owners in Belmont Light service territory.

hardRequirements: Battery storage system must be installed at a residential address in Belmont Light territory.
Standard Interconnection Application process must be followed.
Application must be submitted within six months of installation.
Approved rebate is applied as a bill credit.
Additional ConnectedHomes incentives require approved interconnection, permission to energize, qualifying battery type, and demand-response enrollment.
blockers: Commercial battery projects are referenced separately and are not supported by this residential rebate page.
Battery systems outside Belmont Light service territory do not qualify.
Solar PV alone, EV chargers, and non-battery resilience measures should not match this battery rebate.
ConnectedHomes incentive amounts should not be inferred unless the battery is enrolled and meets additional requirements.
repairs.evidenceText: Belmont Light's battery storage page and application support a residential battery storage rebate, with interconnection and six-month application requirements.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The battery storage match is source-backed for residential Belmont Light customers; separate ConnectedHomes incentives should be modeled as additional conditions, not generalized categories.
